title: Sonic black holes with thick horizons in BECs
authors: Daniel Peñalver, Marco De Vito, Roberto Balbinot, Alessandro Fabbri
abstract: We consider simple one dimensional models of acoustic black holes formed by Bose-Einstein condensates where the flow is stepwise homogeneous. We shall concentrate on the case in which an extended sonic region is present, i.e. a region where the flow velocity equals exactly the speed of sound. These models can be thought of as acoustic black holes with a thick horizon. Particular attention will be devoted to the number of created particles and to the density-density correlation functions, these latter being at present time the experimental tool to identify Hawking like radiation in acoustic black holes.
summary: This paper theoretically models acoustic black holes using Bose-Einstein condensates exhibiting thick sonic horizons. By analyzing wave propagation across flow discontinuities, the authors calculate particle creation rates and correlation functions analogous to Hawking radiation. The results confirm Planckian statistics and provide a detailed theoretical framework for detecting these quantum effects in BEC experiments.
main_problem: The study investigates acoustic black holes formed within Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) that possess thick sonic horizons.
main_result: Particle creation rates exhibit good agreement with Planckian distributions for low frequencies, and correlation functions show distinct peaks corresponding to different pairs of created particles.
method: The analysis uses Bogoliubov theory applied to the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, solving matching conditions across discontinuities separating subsonic/supersonic regions.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional BEC modeled by the GP equation, analyzed in regimes transitioning from subsonic ($|v|<c$) to supersonic ($|v|>c$) flow, featuring a thick sonic horizon where flow velocity equals the speed of sound.
key_observables: Number of created particles and density-density correlation functions (used as experimental diagnostics for Hawking-like radiation).
important_parameters: Flow velocity ($v$), speed of sound ($c$), external potential ($V_{	ext{ext}}$), coupling constant ($g$), and the width/location of discontinuities.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on idealized models, such as assuming constant density and flow velocity across regions, and uses approximations like leading order in frequency ($\omega$).
figures_summary: Figures compare calculated particle numbers against Planckian distributions for Hawking, Partner, and Spectator modes; other figures illustrate 'in' and 'out' mode solutions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the dispersion relation across different flow regimes (subsonic, supersonic, sonic) to applying matching conditions at step-like discontinuities in a multi-region model, culminating in calculations of particle creation rates and correlation functions.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced quantum field theory techniques (Bogoliubov transformations, scattering matrices) to ultracold atomic systems, providing concrete theoretical predictions for observable signatures like Hawking radiation analogues.
